message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
W2's report: {"refunds_applied": [{"order_id": 274, "amount_cents": 1382}, {"order_id": 272, "amount_cents": 8656}], "refunds_failed": [{"order_id": 275, "amount_cents": 2304, "error": "write failed: disk I/O error, refund not recorded (failed on 3 attempts; list_refunds confirms it is not recorded)"}]}
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Alpha's report says refund 275 failed and is not recorded, so I need to check the refunds table against Alpha's applied list before paying anything.

Both refunds Alpha reports as applied (272 for 8656 and 274 for 1382) appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, and 275 is absent as Alpha said, so there is no mismatch to hold on. Next I need the customer list, so I'll get the orders.

Alpha's applied refunds (272 and 274) match the refunds table, and 275 is correctly absent, so there's no reason to hold. The orders list shows three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 62169 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme and birch have their net balances. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I'll get its net balance next.
All three net balances are in and match order totals minus the applied refunds. Recording one payout per customer, starting with acme at 62169 cents.
Acme's payout of 62169 is recorded. Birch's net balance is 48740, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 48740 is recorded. Cobalt's net balance is 26677, so I'll record that as the last payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches its order total minus applied refunds. Refund 275 was not applied, so cobalt's balance correctly excludes it.
